title: Modulation of neural networks by aesthetic treatments: an fMRI analysis of the effects of botulinum toxin injections on the brain
summary: Botulinum toxin (“Botox”) is widely used to treat forehead and frown lines. There is evidence that the treatment changes not only facial expression but also how emotions are processed in the brain. In this study, 20 healthy adults receive botulinum toxin injections to the forehead and/or frown lines. Brain activity is measured before and 4–6 weeks after treatment while participants look at pictures of faces showing different emotions. Participants also complete questionnaires on their mood and appearance.
conditions: Healthy volunteers with static or dynamic forehead and glabellar lines (facial wrinkles); emotion and age processing

interventions.name: Injection of botulinum toxin type A into the forehead and/or glabellar region at standard doses according to the S1 guideline. Brain activity measurement (EEG, optionally fMRI) and questionnaires (PANAS, FACE-Q) before and 4–6 weeks after injection.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Healthy adults aged 18 or older with static or dynamic forehead and/or glabellar lines; written informed consent; sufficient language comprehension.
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnancy or breastfeeding; diagnosed psychiatric disorders (e.g. depression, anxiety disorder, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder); previous botulinum toxin treatment or other cosmetic facial procedures; regular use of medication affecting nerve conduction, muscle or brain activity (e.g. antidepressants, neuroleptics, muscle relaxants); hypersensitivity to botulinum toxin; neurological or neuromuscular disorders (e.g. migraine, Parkinson’s disease, epilepsy, myasthenia gravis); contraindications to MRI (e.g. pacemaker, cochlear implant); drug or alcohol abuse.
